device.category: 16-voice digital FM synthesizer, 61 keys with velocity and aftertouch
device.based_on: Original design, 1983, using John Chowning's FM synthesis licensed from Stanford; two custom chips (YM21280 OPS, YM21290 EGS).

sources.title: Yamaha DX7 Operation Manual
sources.note: Controls, all EDIT and FUNCTION parameters with ranges, programming tutorial, memory, MIDI (in general terms) and specifications. Shows only a few algorithms (3 to 6); the voice data list page is blank in this scan.

sources.title: Ken Shirriff, 'Yamaha DX7 chip reverse-engineering, part 4: how algorithms are implemented'
sources.note: Full algorithm ROM: per-operator modulation source, feedback register and output count (COM). Used to confirm all 32 routings, carriers and feedback loops, and the output level compensation.

sources.title: DX7 MIDI data format (DX7 data sheet and Keyboard, Jan 1987), as transcribed on YamahaMusicians.com
sources.note: Single-voice and 32-voice bulk dump headers, 155-byte voice layout, function parameter numbers 64-77.

sources.title: DX7 Librarian voice list and ROM 1 cartridge listing
sources.note: Names and order of the 32 ROM 1A voices.

sources.title: Yamaha DX7 II FD MIDI implementation chart
sources.note: Comparable controller numbers; the original DX7 manual gives none.

architecture.patch_memory_note: 32 internal voices (battery-backed RAM), 32 on a RAM cartridge, 64 on a ROM cartridge (two banks of 32). Function settings are global, not per voice.
architecture.summary: Each of 16 voices has six sine-wave operators, each with its own frequency (ratio to the key or fixed in Hz), detune, eight-stage rate/level envelope, output level, keyboard level and rate scaling, velocity and amplitude-modulation sensitivity. One of 32 algorithms decides which operators are heard (carriers) and which modulate others, with one adjustable feedback loop. A pitch envelope moves all six together. One LFO (six waves) gives pitch and amplitude modulation, scaled by the mod wheel, foot and breath controllers and aftertouch, which can also bias the envelopes. All programming runs through 32 multi-function buttons and one data entry slider.

modules.name: Keyboard and voice assigner
modules.description: 61 keys (C1-C6) with initial (velocity) and after (pressure) touch; 16-note poly or mono, portamento or glissando, key transpose.

modules.name: Pitch and modulation wheels
modules.description: Spring-return pitch wheel and modulation wheel.

modules.name: LFO
modules.description: One LFO: triangle, saw down, saw up, square, sine or sample and hold; speed, delay, pitch and amplitude depths, key sync.

modules.name: Modulation controllers
modules.description: Combines the LFO's programmed depths (PMD, AMD) with the mod wheel, foot controller, breath controller and aftertouch. Each controller has a RANGE and switches for PITCH (adds LFO pitch modulation), AMPLITUDE (adds LFO amplitude modulation) and EG BIAS (lowers operator levels directly, without the LFO).

modules.name: Pitch EG
modules.description: Four-rate, four-level pitch envelope moving all six operators equally, ±4 octaves (level 50 is no change).

modules.name: Operator 1
modules.panel_section: EDIT: OSCILLATOR / EG / KEYBOARD SCALING / OPERATOR
modules.description: Sine oscillator with its own frequency, envelope and level. Carrier or modulator by algorithm; modulation links are in the algorithms section.

modules.name: Carrier sum
modules.description: Sums the carriers of the current algorithm, each scaled down by the number of carriers so all algorithms play at similar volume.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: DAC and VOLUME slider to the line output and headphones; the VOLUME foot controller jack scales the level.

indicators.label: voice number LED
indicators.function: Two-digit voice number; a decimal point means the voice is being edited; blinks during EDIT/COMPARE.

indicators.label: LCD
indicators.function: 16 x 2 characters: voice name and source, or the current EDIT/FUNCTION parameter, the operator on/off pattern and the current operator.

behaviours.name: Modes
behaviours.rule: PLAY (MEMORY SELECT INTERNAL or CARTRIDGE, then VOICE SELECT 1-32), EDIT (violet labels: voice parameters, DATA ENTRY sets the selected one) and FUNCTION (brown labels: global settings and utilities). Each of the 32 buttons has up to five labels. In EDIT, OPERATOR SELECT chooses which operator per-operator parameters apply to.

behaviours.name: Carriers and modulators
behaviours.rule: In each algorithm, carriers are heard and modulators change their timbre. Raising a modulator's level or envelope brightens the carrier it feeds; key velocity on a modulator changes tone, on a carrier changes volume. Changing algorithm swaps which operators are carriers, so a voice can change completely.

behaviours.name: Operator frequency
behaviours.rule: Ratio mode: frequency = key pitch x (coarse, 0.50 or 1-31) x (1 + fine/100), plus detune ±7. Fixed mode: coarse picks 1, 10, 100 or 1000 Hz and fine multiplies it, ignoring the key. Whole-number ratios give harmonic tones; non-integer ratios give bell-like inharmonic ones.

behaviours.name: Envelopes
behaviours.rule: Each envelope moves to level 1 at rate 1, then level 2 at rate 2, then level 3 at rate 3 and holds there while the key is down; on release it moves to level 4 at rate 4. Rates run 0 (slowest) to 99 (fastest). With all levels at 99 except level 4 at 0 and all rates at 99 the envelope is a square gate. Keyboard rate scaling speeds rates on higher keys.

behaviours.name: Keyboard level scaling
behaviours.rule: Either side of the break point, an operator's level can fall or rise along a linear or exponential curve of set depth: realistic tone changes across the range, or split effects. A boost needs headroom below output level 99.

behaviours.name: Modulation controllers
behaviours.rule: LFO pitch modulation = PMD plus any controller set to PITCH, scaled by the voice's pitch sensitivity; amplitude modulation likewise with AMD, AMPLITUDE and each operator's amplitude sensitivity. EG BIAS lets a controller lower operator levels directly. With zero sensitivity in the voice, the controllers do nothing; with EG BIAS or AMPLITUDE on and a low RANGE, some voices go silent.

behaviours.name: Memory
behaviours.rule: Voices are edited in a buffer and kept only after STORE to an internal or RAM cartridge slot (memory protect off). ROM cartridges hold 64 voices in two banks of 32. Function settings are global and stay when voices change. The internal memory is battery-backed (lithium, 3-5 years).

behaviours.name: Voice name
behaviours.rule: Up to 10 characters, entered with VOICE NAME (button 32): hold CHARACTER and press the buttons carrying the letters. Stored in voice data bytes 145-154.
behaviours.note: Not modelled as a parameter: the schema has no text parameter kind.

behaviours.name: MIDI
behaviours.rule: Notes with velocity, pitch bend, controllers and program changes are always sent and received on the MIDI channel. Voice and function data travel as SysEx only with SYS INFO AVAIL on; MIDI TRANSMIT sends all 32 voices. A second DX7 or a DX9 can be played and programmed from the first.

feedback.note: Feedback returns from the bottom of the stack to its top modulator.
Feedback returns from the bottom of the stack to its top modulator.

algorithms.source: Routings from the DX7 panel chart, cross-checked against the algorithm ROM decoded by Ken Shirriff (modulation source, feedback register and output count per operator).
algorithms.note: Operators are only modulated by higher-numbered operators, and every algorithm has exactly one feedback loop. Carrier outputs are scaled by 1/number of carriers.

single voice dump: 155 bytes + checksum + F7

transmits.note: wheel, breath, foot, sustain, portamento, data entry (inferred)

midi.voice_data_layout: Per operator (operator 6 first, 21 bytes each): rates 1-4, levels 1-4, break point, left depth, right depth, left curve, right curve, rate scaling, amplitude sensitivity, velocity sensitivity, output level, osc mode, coarse, fine, detune. Then pitch EG rates 1-4 and levels 1-4, algorithm, feedback, osc key sync, LFO speed, delay, PMD, AMD, sync, wave, pitch mod sensitivity, transpose, name (10).
midi.note: The manual describes MIDI in general terms only; controller numbers follow the DX7 II implementation chart and the original data sheet.

source_inconsistencies: The manual describes OSC KEY SYNC per operator under MODE/SYNC, but the voice data holds one sync value for the whole voice.
The manual says feedback returns to the same operator 'except in algorithms 4 and 6'; the algorithm ROM shows those loops run through three and two operators respectively.
The feature summary gives Key Transpose 'over a 4 octave range'; the specifications say ±2 octaves. Both describe the same span.

modelling_gaps.detail: Ten characters per voice; the schema has no text parameter kind, so it is described in behaviours.
ROM 1A voices are listed by name only; their 155 values would come from the factory SysEx bank.
Rate-to-time and level-to-dB curves are nonlinear and undocumented here; values stay on the instrument's 0-99 scales.
Not a signal port; described under memory rather than ports.
